jobs.prompt:
TASK: wire four finished read-only modules into Swarm Watch. Do NOT change those modules' exported behavior, and do NOT touch tools/swarm.mjs, package.json, CHANGELOG.md or README.md.
Modules (read them in context): tools/board-peers.mjs (listPeers, createPeerCache, fetchPeer, mergeMachines, publicPeers), tools/handled.mjs (handledForProject), tools/orchestrator-chat.mjs (chatUrlFor), tools/pools-board.mjs (boardPools, stubPools; contract docs/pools-board.md).

A) Multi-machine board (roadmap R-028: projects and orchestrators from the MacBook and the Mac mini on one board; each card shows its machine and swarm version; version drift flagged):
 - tools/watch-server.mjs: GET /api/board accepts `local=1` (query) meaning 'this machine only, no peers'. Pass that flag through to the board snapshot function. Everything else unchanged (token check stays first).
 - tools/watch-cli.mjs createBoardApi: create ONE peer cache per server (createPeerCache()). In the snapshot path, when not local-only: peers = await listPeers(env) (errors -> []); results = await cache.all(peers); BUT every peer fetch must request the peer's LOCAL view: wrap fetchImpl or build the URL so the request is /api/board?local=1 (token still only in the x-watch-token header) — this prevents two boards copying each other forever. Then merged = mergeMachines({ name: os.hostname(), version: versionInfo().version (tools/server-version.mjs), projects: snapshot.projects, orchestrators: snapshot.machine.orchestrator.sessions }, results); also defensively drop any remote project/orchestrator whose own `machine` tag is already set and differs from that peer's machine (an older peer relaying ours). Set snapshot.projects = merged.projects, snapshot.machine.orchestrator.sessions = merged.orchestrators, snapshot.machines = merged.machines, snapshot.drift = merged.drift, snapshot.peers = publicPeers(peers) (never tokens). When there are no peers, still tag local cards with { machine: os.hostname(), version } and set machines = [that one], drift = { drifted: false, versions: [version] }. Machine totals stay local-only (do not add remote money into this machine's totals; label that in the UI).
 - The /api/project, /api/live and run routes stay local-only; a remote project card must not link to them.
 - tools/watch-assets/board.js renderProjects: each row/card shows a small machine tag `p.machine` + ' · v' + p.version; when p.versionDrift add a pill 'version drift' (warn) with title 'this machine runs vX; newest is vY'; remote cards (p.remote) link their name to the peer's board base URL from snapshot.peers (match by machine/name) with target=_blank rel=noopener and NO token in the href, title 'open on <machine>'; local ones keep today's links. Above the projects table add one line listing machines: 'Machines: mini (v1.156.0) · mbp (v1.155.0, unreachable)' and, when snapshot.drift.drifted, a warn pill 'version drift: <versions>'. Add 'Totals above are this machine only' note under the top tiles when machines.length > 1.
 - tools/watch-assets/orchestrator-view.js: show the session's machine tag (s.machine) in the card name line when present.

B) Handled for you (policy engine auto-decisions):
 - tools/board-data.mjs projectOverview adds `handled: { today, week }` from handledForProject(project.root, { now }) (null on error); projectDetail adds `handled` (the full result, limit 20).
 - board.js: when p.handled && p.handled.today, a sub line 'N handled for you today' in the row and card.
 - tools/watch-assets/project.html: a card section id 'handled' aria-label 'Handled for you' (h2 'Handled for you') in the Overview pane after Split quality; project.js renders: header 'N today · M this week', then the items (time, rule, requestKind requestId, reason) or 'Nothing handled yet. The policy engine logs auto-decisions here.' textContent only.

C) Open chat link (roadmap R-029):
 - tools/board-orchestrator.mjs: for each shown session, add `chatUrl: chatUrlFor(fullSessionId)` (use the session's full id before it is shortened to 8 chars; null when none). Injectable `chatUrl` function option for tests.
 - orchestrator-view.js: when s.chatUrl matches /^https:\/\/claude\.ai\/code\/session_[A-Za-z0-9]{10,80}$/ add an <a> 'Open chat' with href = s.chatUrl, target=_blank, rel='noopener noreferrer'; never otherwise.

D) Capacity pools:
 - watch-cli.mjs snapshot path: snapshot.pools = await boardPools({ now, stubInput: { workers: <the workersHeld result already computed for the snapshot>, laneRows: <the laneUsage rows already computed for the snapshot>, hosts: enabled hosts from loadLocalConfig({ env }).hosts (array of {id, kind, capacity, enabled}; [] if missing) } }) — find where the snapshot stores workers and lane rows and reuse them, do not recompute differently. Errors -> { source: 'stub', pools: [], at }.
 - tools/watch-assets/board.html: in the Agents tab (find the agents pane) add a card 'Capacity pools' with a table (id poolsTable) and a note (id poolsNote). board.js renderPools(data.pools): columns Pool, Kind, Limit, In use, Status; Status = 'capped: ' + why (warn/bad pill) or 'ok'; a meter for limit>0; note 'Source: pools.mjs' or 'Source: stub from lane store and config (pools.mjs not installed yet)'. Call it where the Agents tab renders.
All DOM text via textContent/setAttribute; never innerHTML.
Tests: extend tests/board-page.test.mjs (or tests/watch-ui.test.mjs where createBoardApi is tested) with: snapshot with no peers tags local projects with machine+version and drift false; with an injected fake peer cache/fetch returning a remote project at an older version, merged projects include it with remote true and versionDrift true, the peer request URL contains local=1 and the token only appears in the header, and snapshot.peers has no token; /api/board?local=1 skips peers; projectDetail.handled reads an auto-decision line from events.ndjson; projectOrchestrator adds chatUrl from an injected function; snapshot.pools has source 'stub' and a machine pool. Make injection points (peer cache, listPeers, chatUrl) options of createBoardApi / projectOrchestrator so tests never touch the network or the real home. Run `node --import ./tests/_isolate-config.mjs --test tests/board-page.test.mjs tests/watch-ui.test.mjs tests/board.test.mjs tests/orchestrator-lane.test.mjs tests/board-peers.test.mjs tests/handled.test.mjs tests/orchestrator-chat.test.mjs tests/pools-board.test.mjs tests/board-nav.test.mjs` and `node tools/check-package.mjs`. tests/watch-server.test.mjs is context: keep it green and run it too. Tests in ignoreTests use these files for unrelated behavior; the coordinator runs the full suite after integration.
